name: Volatility-spike capitulation reversion (15m)
rationale: When realized volatility SPIKES above a floor AND the band z-score is deeply negative on 15m, the market is in capitulation — forced sellers dumping into a vol shock. That is precisely where the sharpest mean-reversion bounces occur once the liquidation wave clears. We buy the panic. The other side is the margin-called holder liquidated at the worst price. Edge persists because capitulation overshoots are violent but short-lived, and the bounce premium is paid by the forced seller. Distinct from the calm-regime washout spec: this REQUIRES high vol (the panic), not low vol. Disconfirmer: exits when the z-score reverts toward zero, or the stop fires if the capitulation extends into a sustained crash.
catalyst: capitulation — deep band dislocation during a volatility spike
